en.t: What is the opposite of shame? Shamelessness.

units.source_text: 是流行漫畫家上司幾太。」「那堀木正雄呢？」

en.t: The popular manga artist Ueji Ikuta. And what about Horiki Masao?

units.source_text: 說到這兒，漸漸地我們倆再也笑不出來，

en.t: At that point, little by little, neither of us could laugh anymore,

units.source_text: 心情變得鬱悶不堪，腦袋裡好像充滿了玻璃碎片，那是燒酒醉意中特有的感覺。

en.t: our mood grew unbearably gloomy, as if our heads were filled with shards of glass, that feeling peculiar to being drunk on shochu.

units.source_text: 「你別臭美，我還沒有像你，遭受過被捆綁關押的恥辱呢。」

en.t: Do not get so full of yourself. I have never suffered the disgrace of being bound and locked up the way you have.

units.source_text: 原來堀木在心中並未真正把我當人看，

en.t: So Horiki had never truly regarded me as a human being in his heart,

units.source_text: 他只是把我當作了自殺未遂、不知恥辱的白痴，

en.t: he merely saw me as a shameless idiot who had failed at suicide,

units.source_text: 也就是所謂的「行屍走肉」，

en.t: in other words, what people call a living corpse,

units.source_text: 他只是為了取樂自己，最大限度地能利用我就利用，

en.t: and simply used me as much as he could for his own amusement,

units.source_text: 我們僅是這種程度的「交友」而已。

en.t: that was all our friendship amounted to.
